n: Instead of rejoicing, Jonah is furious that God spared Nineveh. The most successful preacher in the Bible is upset by his success.

f.g: Literally “it was evil to Jonah, a great evil” — a play on the “evil” God had just withheld.

n: Jonah finally reveals why he ran: he knew God was gracious and merciful and would forgive the Ninevites. He quotes God’s own description of Himself — as a complaint!

f.w: a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger

n: Jonah asks God to take his life, echoing Elijah’s despair under the juniper tree, but for a far less worthy reason.

f.w: it is better for me to die than to live

n: God responds gently with a question: “Is it right for you to be angry?” Like a patient teacher, He invites Jonah to examine his heart.

f.w: Doest thou well to be angry?

n: Jonah leaves, builds a shelter east of the city, and waits to see whether Nineveh will be destroyed after all.

f.g: A simple hut made of branches.

n: God makes a leafy plant grow quickly over Jonah to shade him. Jonah is very happy about the plant — the only time the book says he is glad.

f.g: Hebrew qiqayon — probably the castor-oil plant, a fast-growing shrub with broad leaves.
Appointed — the same verb used for the fish (1:17), the worm, and the wind.

n: Next morning God sends a worm to attack the plant, and it withers.
Then God sends a scorching east wind. With the sun beating on his head, Jonah grows faint and again wishes to die.

f.g: A hot desert wind, sometimes called a sirocco.

n: God asks again: “Is it right to be angry about the plant?” Jonah snaps back, “Yes, angry enough to die!”

f.g: Angry enough to die — a stubborn, sulking reply.

n: The Lord draws the lesson: you cared about a plant you didn’t plant or tend, which lived only a night.

f.w: Thou hast had pity on the gourd
f.g: Jonah’s concern was really for his own comfort.

n: Shouldn’t I care about Nineveh, with more than 120,000 people who don’t know right from left — and many animals? The book ends with God’s question hanging, inviting every reader to share God’s compassion for all people.

f.g: A score is 20; sixscore thousand is 120,000.

f.w: cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand
f.g: Morally or spiritually untaught — or possibly small children.
